subject: Observability & Evals — discovery notes, success criteria, and next steps
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen@finhealth.ai>, Ben Ortiz <ben.ortiz@finhealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Observability & Evals — discovery notes, success criteria, and next steps

Hi Ellen / Ben —

Thanks again for the productive chat today. Quick summary from my side while it's fresh so we all have a single source of truth. Below are the key pain points you mentioned, the measurable success criteria we discussed, and proposed next steps.

Pain points we heard
- Low confidence in model performance drift post-deployment; ops discovers issues only after customer impact.
- Lack of a standardized evaluation suite for new prompt sets (no golden prompt baseline).
- No consolidated dashboard tying latency/cost/per-token quality signals to business KPIs.
- Tracing hooks are partially instrumented today; KV-cache hits and per-request token counts aren't surfaced.

Current stack (what you told us)
- Serving: internal inference infra on GCP with a mix of CPU fallback and small GPU pool.
- Monitoring: Prometheus + Grafana for infra; some bespoke logs for model outputs stored in S3.
- CI: unit tests + manual evals before PR merges, no automated regression gate.

Success criteria (agreed on call)
- Alerting: auto-detect a >5% drop in golden-prompt pass-rate within a 24h window (pilot).
- Visibility: a single observability dashboard showing error-rate, 95th/99th latency, cost per token, and golden-prompt accuracy for top-10 routes.
- Rollout guardrails: canary rollout with automatic rollback on quality regression or latency SLO breach.
- Time-to-troubleshoot: reduce median time-to-root-cause from ~6 hours to <90 minutes for inference incidents.

Proposed next steps
1) We will share a short playbook (attached) that maps Redwood observability features to your stack and a recommended rollout plan.
2) FinHealth to share a sanitized sample of 24–72 hours of prediction logs (S3 link or secure upload) so we can sketch a dashboard and golden-prompt set.
3) Schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive with your TechOps and our reliability engineer to review tracing hooks and KV cache metrics — suggested window: next Tues/Thu morning PT.
4) We'll draft a mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones and owners — I attached a worksheet and filled the first tab with what we covered.

If the items above look right, reply with which deep-dive slot works and whether we should use your secure S3 share or a temporary upload link.

Quick note on scope/cost: for the pilot we're recommending Redwood Optimize + a Dedicated-grade observability config to ensure consistent latency sampling; I can put numbers against that after the deep-dive.

Thanks again — Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

redwood.ai

Rishi —

Thanks for the clear summary and for putting that playbook together so quickly. Confirming a few points and answering your asks:

- We can provide a 48-hour slice of anonymized prediction logs (S3 bucket) by COB Tuesday; will include request metadata, model responses, and timing.

Two questions from our side:
1) What level of trace sampling does Redwood recommend initially (full trace vs. 10% sampling) to avoid cost blow-up?
2) For the golden-prompt suite, what's the minimum set we should prepare to get meaningful regression detection?

Ben — looping you for any security/upload constraints.

Cheers,

Subject: Re: Observability & Evals — discovery notes, success criteria, and next steps

Hi Ellen / Ben —

Great — Thurs 28th 10:00 PT works for our reliability engineer and myself. I'll send a calendar invite in a moment. Quick answers to your two questions:

1) Trace sampling recommendation: start at 5–10% for end-to-end traces and 100% for request/response metadata (latency, token counts, KV cache hit/miss). That usually gives a good signal without the storage/cost impact of full tracing. We can toggle sampling dynamically if we need to investigate a regression.

2) Golden-prompt minimum set: 50 prompts that cover your top 3 routes (customer triage, payment reconciliation, claims summarization). Aim for 2–3 known-good outputs per prompt (acceptable variability documented). We can help curate this — if you share top routes we'll draft the initial set.

Also attaching a short checklist that maps the logs you mentioned to the fields our dashboard consumes.

Best,
Marissa
